arithmetic.formula_note: The clamp runs LAST in Organism::step (commit b4d116e), so the step ends on capacity whenever income covers the spend. The spend does not enter the ceiling; it only decides whether it is reached.
arithmetic.superseded_note: That was correct while min(capacity) ran right after the income. The 2026-11-13 run of this experiment failed on it: A measured 100.0 not 99.37, B 10.0 not 9.37, C 10.0 not 9.25. The failure was correct — the code and the text had diverged.
arithmetic.balance_note: The balance must stay positive or the organism dies before reaching the ceiling. At damage_rate=0.10 the balance is +0.05.
arithmetic.steps_note: An arm reaches its ceiling only after (ceiling - 5.0) / balance steps. A needs 559 steps; the run is 1200. C needs 100.

fires.evidence: A: max energy 100.0000 vs its own predicted ceiling 100.0000 — must have REACHED the ceiling, not merely grown past B's

silent.evidence: B: max energy 10.0000 vs predicted 10.0000 — must match

specific.evidence: C: ceiling moved by 0.000000 when damage_rate went 0.02 -> 0.10; the formula says 0.000000 because the clamp is last. An income/spend equilibrium would have moved it by 0.120000.

verdict.reason: all three arms sit on their capacity; the ceiling is capacity, not an income/spend equilibrium and not capacity minus the spend

limitations: One seed. Reproducibility across seeds is not checked here.
One policy (`stay`). `remember` and `random` are not tested in this run.
The formula is read off `Organism::step`; if that code changes, the arithmetic must be re-derived. It has already changed once (b4d116e).
The ceiling is a property of the model's update order, not of life. It says nothing about whether an organism SHOULD be able to sit at its capacity; it says only that this model lets it.
The `specific` control cannot distinguish `E_max = capacity` from any other formula that does not contain the spend. It rules out the income/spend equilibrium, not every alternative.
